item.title: New planning applications submitted across Fenland
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
New planning applications submitted across Fenland
A range of new planning applications have been submitted to local councils across the Fens. Among the proposals is a project in Wisbech at 13 Alexandra Road, where plans have been lodged to convert and extend a building to create three houses and six flats.
Other notable applications include the construction of three new homes on land south of 10 Sutton Road in Leverington, and a proposal for a new dwelling at Parsons Lane Drove. Additionally, the local fire station on Churchill Road in Wisbech has applied to install a back-up generator. Residents can view the full list of planning submissions through their local council’s planning portal.

item.title: King’s Lynn law firm raises over £2,000 for local charities
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn law firm raises over £2,000 for local charities
A charity quiz hosted by law firm Fraser Dawbarns has raised a total of £2,520. The event, held at King’s Lynn Town Hall on October 22, saw teams compete to support two local causes: Breast of Friends and the West Norfolk Autism Group. Each charity received a donation of £1,260.
The evening was hosted by the Mayor of West Norfolk, Councillor Steve Bearshaw. On the leaderboard, the team from Complete Commercial Finance secured the top spot. Both charities have been selected to receive ongoing support from the firm until April 2028. Organisers have already confirmed that the next annual quiz will take place on October 14, 2027.

item.title: Wisbech residents gather for Remembrance Sunday parade
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech residents gather for Remembrance Sunday parade
Crowds gathered in Wisbech town centre on Sunday morning to mark Remembrance Day. The annual event, organised by the Town Council and the local branch of the Royal British Legion, saw cadets, armed forces members, and the public parade towards the war memorial at The Crescent.
Mayor Lucie Foice-Beard attended the service, which included the laying of wreaths and a two-minute silence at 11am. Among those paying their respects was 103-year-old veteran Stanley Eastgate. Local representatives praised the community for their support of the commemorations, which featured poppy displays throughout the town to honour those who lost their lives in service.

item.title: Inquest concludes into the death of North Lynn woman
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Inquest concludes into the death of North Lynn woman
An inquest at Norfolk Coroner’s Court has concluded that the death of 57-year-old Janina Daunaraviciute was alcohol-related. The North Lynn resident was found dead in her garden on Raby Avenue in the early hours of June 26. The court heard that Ms Daunaraviciute, an agency worker, had been struggling following the death of her husband last year. Her daughter told the hearing that her mother had appeared normal earlier that evening. A post-mortem examination confirmed the cause of death as hanging, with toxicology reports showing high levels of alcohol in her system. Area coroner Johanna Thompson offered her condolences to the family. If you are affected by these issues, you can contact Samaritans on 116 123.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/mother-appeared-normal-moments-before-she-took-her-own-lif-9490578/

item.description:

King’s Lynn man fined after failed shoplifting attempt
A 34-year-old father from Fairstead has been fined following a failed attempt to steal groceries from the Asda store in South Wootton. Brendon Smith, of William Booth Road, pleaded guilty at Lynn Magistrates’ Court to the theft of goods worth more than £400.
The court heard that on September 15, Smith and another man were intercepted by a security guard while attempting to drive away with the stolen items. The groceries were recovered at the scene. Smith was ordered to pay a total of £157, covering an £80 fine, a victim surcharge, and court costs. His co-offender did not appear in court.

item.title: North Lynn mechanic banned after A17 traffic stop
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
North Lynn mechanic banned after A17 traffic stop
A North Lynn mechanic has been disqualified from driving for six months following an incident on the A17. Police stopped 39-year-old Jevgenijus Levinskas on April 20 after noticing he was driving a vehicle insured to someone else. Officers discovered Levinskas was using false number plates to conceal the fact that he did not hold a valid driving licence. A search of the car also uncovered a quantity of the Class B drug Cathinone. At Lynn Magistrates’ Court, Levinskas pleaded guilty to multiple driving offences and drug possession. He was issued a £120 fine and received six penalty points, resulting in a driving ban after exceeding the 12-point limit.

Mr Ogle has been released on unconditional bail, while Ms Kennett remains on bail with conditions preventing her from contacting the alleged victim of the threatening behaviour.

item.title: King’s Lynn runner to complete 45 festive fancy dress runs
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn runner to complete 45 festive fancy dress runs
A King’s Lynn athlete is preparing for a demanding fundraising challenge throughout December. Matty Parker, a member of Ryston Runners, plans to complete 45 separate 5km runs while wearing a different fancy dress costume for each outing. The initiative, titled December Dashes, aims to raise funds and awareness for the charity Caring Together, which supports unpaid carers.
Mr. Parker intends to visit various locations across the region, including St Ives and Swaffham, and hopes to be joined by fellow runners. His challenge concludes on New Year’s Eve at RAF Marham. Supporters can contribute to his fundraising appeal via the JustGiving website.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/fancy-dress-festive-challenge-of-45-5km-runs-in-december-9490384/
